evidence_summary: Fossil evidence includes a Tyrannosaurus rex tooth embedded in healed hadrosaur vertebrae, demonstrating an attack on living prey closely comparable to Edmontosaurus annectens.
Tyrannosaur bite traces and healed injuries on Triceratops remains support possible predator-prey interaction, although some feeding traces may represent scavenging rather than active predation.
Tyrannosaurus rex fossils preserve feeding traces attributed to other T. rex individuals, supporting cannibalistic feeding or scavenging of members of the same species.
